Medical and Surgical Management
The primary medical treatment of esophageal reflux is sup-
pression of acid secretion. The aim in acid-suppression ther-
apy is to raise the gastric pH above 4 during periods when 
reflux is most likely to occur. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), 
which decrease acid production by the gastric parietal cell, 
have been associated with superior healing rates and de-
creased relapses (Katz et al, 2013). Milder forms of reflux are
